title: Solving Dual-Write Cache Invalidation Races
prompt: Your user profile service uses classic Cache-Aside against PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 7 (30,000 reads/sec, 800 writes/sec). Writers execute `UPDATE profiles ...` followed by `redis.del(key)`. Readers on a cache miss execute `SELECT ...` and then `redis.set(key, val, ex=3600)`. Under concurrent load, ~0.05% of profile updates (~35/day) revert to old values in Redis for up to 1 hour because a concurrent cache-miss reader fetched `v1` before the writer committed `v2`, paused on GC/network, and wrote `v1` into Redis after the writer's `DEL`. Redesign the read/write caching protocol to make stale cache repopulation impossible.

spark.summary: Under Cache-Aside, a slow cache-miss reader that fetches `v1` from the DB can get preempted while a writer commits `v2` and deletes the cache, after which the reader writes stale `v1` back into Redis.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, eliminate Cache-Aside read-write races using monotonic row `version` Compare-And-Swap (Lua CAS) in Redis or by moving cache population/invalidation to a single-writer CDC stream.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Preempted Cache-Miss Reader Overwrites Newer Commit v2 (Miss Reader -> Redis 7 -> Postgres 16 -> Writer (v2)); Monotonic Version Lua CAS Rejects Stale v1 Fills (Reader / Writer -> Redis Lua CAS -> Version Tombstone -> PostgreSQL 16 (BIGINT version)).

learningJourney.markdownContent:
```lua
-- Atomic Redis Lua CAS: only write if incoming version > cached/tombstone version
local key = KEYS[1]
local new_ver = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local payload = ARGV[2]
local ttl = tonumber(ARGV[3])

local cur = redis.call("HGET", key, "ver")
if cur and tonumber(cur) >= new_ver then
  return 0
end
redis.call("HSET", key, "ver", new_ver, "data", payload)
redis.call("EXPIRE", key, ttl)
return 1
```
